newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends weaker despite intervention.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends weaker despite intervention.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended weaker on Friday at C$1.3835 (US$0.7228) from Thursday's close of C$1.3765 (US$0.7264) despite intervention by the Bank of Canada, dealers said.
* They said the Bank of Canada intervened to buy Canadian dollars around C$1.3844 (US$0.7223) after the currency eased on U.S. economic data.

The U.S. Labor Department reported payrolls rose by just 138,000 in May, less than the 219,000 expected by economists, but a rise in April was revised up to 323,000 from a previously reported 142,000 jobs. U.S. unemployment fell to its lowest level in 23 years in May, falling to 4.8 percent from 4.9 percent a month earlier.

Dealers said the currency slipped as a result of the underlying inflationary trends which appeared in the economic numbers. Although the headline numbers are lower, they said the underlying trends could push the Federal Open Market Committee to hike U.S. rates soon after its July 1-2 meeting.

In other economic news, Canada released unemployment data earlier this morning showing a small drop in the unemployment rate to 9.5 percent in May from 9.6 percent in April. The decrease was in line with a Reuters survey of economists forecast. Statistics Canada also reported that full-time employment rose by 61,300 in May, compared with an increase of 33,000 in April.
On the crosses, Canada's dollar fell to 82.56 yen from Thursday's close of 83.94 yen and slid to 1.2466 marks from Thursday's 1.2544 marks.
